correctness.rationale: The explicit stages have a verified O(h^3) smooth local error. Their frozen-scalar companion is an exact affine function of the Chebyshev parameter. The positive-definite P has determinant 4/45. Exact endpoint identities, matrix convexity, and the substitution 1-t=x(4-x)/2 give the claimed all-sequence product bound. At x=2 the squared eigenvalue modulus is 1/5, proving coefficient optimality; equality and the unit boundary eigenvector force Q proportional to P. The D(t) determinant and lower-right principal minor give full Schur-window contractivity. The exact standard-library verifier passed 2932 checks; infinite assertions follow from analytic identities, not enumeration.

value.rationale: Time-varying scalar dissipation and switched modes are natural stress tests for stabilized multistep integrators. Frozen-mode Schur stability is not generally sufficient for arbitrary matrix products; the rational scheme admits an exact common energy over every frozen-stable parameter. A sharp optimal coefficient and unique metric offer a usable quantitative stability budget rather than a small numerical improvement, arbitrary slice, or rebranded known order condition.
